content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm working with a home automation setup that uses a [version_no] controller as the main device and multiple [product_name] units to manage various tasks. Everything was running smoothly until I switched out an older [product_name] with one that has FS.04 firmware. The internal software was left unchanged. After replacing the unit, I noticed some unusual behavior with gate control. When I checked the [product_name] running FS.04 firmware, I found that the network inputs were unstable. To troubleshoot, I updated the program inside my main controller to constantly drive a specific network input on the [product_name] to true/high. When I monitored the [product_name], I observed that the input would activate, then after about 2 seconds go low, and later cycle back to true repeatedly. I'm using [product_name] V13 SP2 for the controller and [product_name] V8.0 for the [product_name]. Any ideas or suggestions on resolving this issue are much appreciated. Kind regards, [user_name]
So you're using the software [product_name] 8.0? For a unit with FS4 firmware, you need at least [product_name] V8.1.

I recommend updating your software to the latest version V8.2 (as mentioned by [user_name], you need at least V8.1). Check that the [product_name] device also has the most recent firmware; sometimes new devices might have older firmware if they’re older stock. I've managed several projects with networked [product_name] units and [version_no] controllers, working on dedicated networks for controllers only, and haven’t encountered your issue. I suggest uploading the program with the newer software (V8.2 or V8.1) and confirming that the correct device model is selected. Also remember to verify the condition of your network cables—a faulty cable can cause intermittent issues and is often hard to identify. Using a network tester helps ensure solid connections.

Hi all, Sorry for my late reply. The software was actually developed in [product_name] v8.1, since it's not possible to program a FS4.0 unit with v8.0. I've now updated to [product_name] v8.2, but the issue persists. I'm confident the network cables are fine, as I haven’t seen this problem with other units on the same network and at similar distances. For now, I need to pause further troubleshooting as I’m working on a new project. I’ll run more tests in the future and share any updates. [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered unstable network input issues on a [product_name] module (FS.04) after replacing an older unit, though the logic software remained unchanged. While software and firmware versions are cited as likely causes, updating to recommended versions did not resolve the instability, suggesting possible compatibility or device-specific challenges. Users highlighted the importance of matching software and firmware versions, and pointed out that similar systems operate reliably elsewhere, which suggests inconsistency in performance.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks dependable and stable network input performance on the [product_name] module with FS.04 firmware after the upgrade, expecting it to function just as reliably as with previous module versions, even with unchanged system setup.
